title: KV fragmentation savings explorer (scenario workbook)
content:
Purpose:
Explore how key-value (KV) cache fragmentation across customers, model versions, and prompt-length cohorts affects hit rate elasticity and unit cost. This workbook is an exploratory sheet (not yet validated) intended to produce rough order-of-magnitude savings and candidate heuristics for the Optimize UX and autoscaler rules.

High-level takeaway (preview):
- Fragmentation can reduce effective hit rate by 6–40% depending on how aggressively we isolate per-customer state and per-model session TTLs.
- For multi-tenant Dedicated pockets, modest coalescing policies (merge cold namespaces with shared short-term cache) recoup 30–60% of fragmented loss without material correctness risk.
- Sparse-prefetch (targeted warm on top-n prompts) yields 2–8% incremental hit improvement for heavy-tail customers; good ROI when prefetch work is throttled by cost-per-prefetch < $0.00012/token equivalent.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Base token cost (inference) = $0.0009 per token (hosted median profile).
- Average response length = 50 tokens; average prompt length = 30 tokens.
- Effective tokens served per request (runtime) includes prompt+gen and internal KV ops.
- Baseline global KV hit rate for a single large shared pool = 28%.
- Fragmentation factors: number of isolated namespaces (N), state-per-namespace (S, tokens), TTL skew.

Key definitions used in scenarios:
- Fragmentation penalty (F): proportional hit-rate lost when caches are split into N namespaces with low cross-namespace reuse. Modeled as F = 1 - (1 / sqrt(N)) * locality_factor. locality_factor in [0.5,1.0].
- Sparse-prefetch: targeted pre-warm of top-K tokens for a namespace when first seen; cost accounted as prefetch tokens * expected reuse within TTL.

Scenario table (select rows from sheet):
Scenario | N(namespaces) | locality_factor | Baseline hit% | Effective hit% | Prefetch? | Projected unit cost delta
Base shared pool | 1 | 1.0 | 28% | 28% | no | $0.0000
Customer-isolation | 100 | 0.6 | 28% | 11% | no | +$0.00046 (↑52%)
Per-model+customer | 400 | 0.5 | 28% | 6% | no | +$0.00064 (↑71%)
Coalesced-eligible | 100 | 0.6 | 28% | 18% | no | +$0.00024 (↑28%)
Sparse-prefetch-top50 | 100 | 0.6 | 11% | 17% | yes | +$0.00010 (net +)
Aggressive-prefetch | 400 | 0.5 | 6% | 14% | yes | +$0.00005 (net +)

Notes on table calculations (quick):
- Effective hit% = Baseline hit% * (1 - F) + prefetch_delta. F computed from N and locality_factor.
- Projected unit cost delta uses simplified model: delta = token_cost * ( (1 - hit_after) - (1 - hit_before) ) * avg_gen_tokens. Positive means more cost vs baseline. Prefetch cost subtracted in 'net' variants.

Micro-experiments sketched (next steps for validation):
1) Synthetic split test: fork cache namespace into X logical namespaces in a staging Dedicated cluster; replay 7 days of production trace (sample) and measure per-namespace hit curves.
   - Output: empirical fragmentation penalty by namespace size and TTL.
2) Prefetch pilot: implement a low-risk prefetch run for 5 enterprise customers (top-50 prompt signatures) behind feature flag. Measure reuse within TTL and additional downstream latency.
3) Coalescing heuristic A/B: allow per-customer ephemeral namespaces to collapse into a short-term shared pool for requests with < 3 unique conversation ids in last 10 minutes. Compare correctness regressions vs cost.

Risk / open questions:
- Privacy/regulatory: some customers may require strict namespace isolation; heuristics must be opt-out and surfaced as tradeoffs in Console.
- Correctness: merging namespaces could leak prompt-resident state in edge cases; need strong conservative matching criteria and monitoring.
- Instrumentation gaps: we currently lack high-fidelity namespace-level hit metrics across model variants; trace sampling needed.

Suggested deliverables and owners:
- Simulation harness (eng-applied-ml): Evan Zhou — implement fragmentation generator + hit-rate model (2 sprints).
- Prefetch pilot feature flag (serving-runtime + product): Marcus Lee + Asha Patel — 3-week pilot.
- Console UX microcopy + rollout toggle (product): Sofia Ramirez — align messaging and compliance flags.

Appendix: quick sensitivity matrices (sheet tabs planned)
- sensitivity-by-namespace-count: sweep N from 1..1000, locality_factor 0.4..1.0
- prefetch-cost-threshold: vary prefetch cost per token and expected reuse (1..10 reuses)
- per-customer-tail: segment customers by 95/5 tail and simulate per-tenant ROI

Scratch formulas (for reproducibility):
- F = 1 - (1 / sqrt(N)) * locality_factor
- prefetch_delta = min( max_reuse * prefetch_tokens / (avg_gen_tokens), theoretical_headroom ) * baseline_hit
- unit_delta = token_cost * avg_gen_tokens * ( (1 - hit_after) - (1 - hit_before) ) - prefetch_cost

Bottom line guidance (what to recommend now):
- For Dedicated customers with many small namespaces, default to a conservative coalescing policy for short-lived conversation state (TTL < 5m) to recover ~30–50% of fragmentation loss; expose as a toggle with clear privacy implications.
- Run a focused prefetch pilot only for customers with heavy-tail prompt reuse and cap prefetch token budget per day. Prefetch for large shared pools where ROI is provably positive.
- Prioritize building namespace-level hit telemetry before wide rollout.
